newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE probes embezzlement charges against Jordanian.
newsitem.headline: UAE probes embezzlement charges against Jordanian.

text.p: Dubai authorities are investigating allegations that a Jordanian had embezzled money while working in the office of the ruler of the Gulf Arab emirate, diplomats said on Monday.

They said the Jordanian national had "suddenly" fled the emirate three months ago but was arrested by Egyptian security forces in Cairo last week at the request of the United Arab Emirates. He was taken straight to jail after arriving in Dubai on Sunday.

The man, born in the now Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip, had worked at the Emiri office of Sheikh Maktoum bin Rashid al-Maktoum -- also UAE Vice-President and Prime Minister -- for over 18 years as a senior financial administrator.
The UAE al-Ittihad daily said the man had embezzled up to 12 million dirhams ($3.2 million).

"...The Jordanian citizen was working for an official department and some financial irregularities occured," Jordanian Consul-General in Dubai, Mashhour al-Zaben, told Reuters. "They (authorities) asked for his handover (from Egypt) and the law will now take its course."
